name: Amazon Neptune
model: Managed graph database: property graphs (Gremlin, openCypher) and RDF graphs (SPARQL) in one service
engine_note: Graph stored as quads in three indexes (SPOG, POGS, GPSO) on the shared, replicated storage layer AWS also uses for Aurora
consistency: Read-only queries: snapshot isolation. Mutations: read committed plus range locks, so no non-repeatable or phantom reads; conflicts wait up to 60 s then roll back. Read replicas are snapshot-consistent but can lag the writer.
scaling: One writer plus up to 15 read replicas on shared storage that grows automatically; Neptune Serverless scales capacity; Neptune Analytics loads graphs in memory for analytics.
version_note: Latest engine release; patch 1.4.7.1 followed on 2026-09-16 for the 1.4.7 line.
reach: Reach for it when you are on AWS, need a managed graph with no servers to run, or need RDF and SPARQL as well as property graphs.
avoid: Avoid if you are not on AWS or want Neo4j's tooling; under high write load expect a few percent of writes to fail on false lock conflicts and retry.
escape: managed multi-hop graph queries on AWS without running a graph cluster yourself
chat: Knowledge graph of entities and documents behind chat retrieval, for teams already all-in on AWS.
notes: Isolation and the '3-4% of write queries fail because of false conflicts' figure are quoted from the transactions page (fetched 2026-10-04). 'Same storage layer as Aurora' and '15 read replicas' are from the Neptune overview docs, not re-fetched today. No Jepsen analysis.
